# criblio_monitor_silence (Resource)

MonitorSilence Resource

Manages a muting rule for an existing customer-metrics monitor. Configure begin and expiration timestamps in Unix milliseconds. Cribl sets creation time and creator; updates preserve those audit values. Expired rules may be removed by Cribl.

A silence mutes all notifications for its monitor, across every series. Selective muting with `tags` or `alert_instance_id` is unsupported by the Metrics API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Use an existing metrics dataset and a PromQL expression available in it.
resource "criblio_monitor" "cpu_high" {
  id         = "silence-example-cpu-high"
  name       = "CPU High"
  dataset_id = "metrics"
  enabled    = true
  type       = "threshold"
  managed_by = "terraform"
  silence    = []

  monitor_policy_notification_config = {
    type    = "policy"
    enabled = false
    config  = []
  }

  query = {
    A = {
      mode       = "promql"
      dataset_id = "metrics"
      promql     = "cpu_usage_percent"
    }
  }

  expr = []

  firing_condition = {
    fire_delay  = 300
    clear_delay = 60
  }

  firing_rule = {
    label = "A"
    threshold = [{
      severity        = "warning"
      limit           = 80
      operator        = "gt"
      included_tags   = []
      excluded_tags   = []
      times_triggered = 1
    }]
  }

  aetos_metadata        = {}
  priority_scalar_value = { value = "P3" }
  team_scalar_value     = { value = "" }
}

resource "criblio_monitor_silence" "example" {
  id          = "maintenance-window"
  monitor_id  = criblio_monitor.cpu_high.id
  name        = "Maintenance window"
  description = "Mute all alerts for this monitor during maintenance"
  # Set a fixed current window before applying; values are Unix milliseconds.
  # Future windows can be excluded by the backend list endpoint.
  begins_at      = 1793325780159 # 2026-10-30 02:03:00.159 UTC.
  expires_at     = 1793329380159 # One hour after begins_at.
  duration_type  = "relative"
  duration_value = 1
  duration_unit  = "hours"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tools/codegen -->
## Schema

### Required

- `begins_at` (Integer) Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the Silence starts muting notifications.
- `expires_at` (Integer) Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the Silence stops muting notifications.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the Silence.
- `monitor_id` (String) The <code>id</code> of the Monitor Configuration whose notifications this Silence mutes. All of the Monitor's notifications are muted, for every series.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description of the Silence.
- `duration_type` (String) Records which duration picker mode the Metrics UI used to set the window. Does not change what the Silence mutes; <code>begins_at</code> and <code>expires_at</code> decide that.
- `duration_unit` (String) Records the unit for a relative duration in the Metrics UI. Does not change what the Silence mutes.
- `duration_value` (Integer) Records the number for a relative duration in the Metrics UI, such as <code>2</code> for two hours. Does not change what the Silence mutes.
- `name` (String) Optional display name for the Silence.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Integer) Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the Silence was created. Set by the server; a value sent in a request is ignored.
- `created_by` (String) Username of who created the Silence. Set by the server; a value sent in a request is ignored.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = criblio_monitor_silence.my_criblio_monitor_silence
  id = "example"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import criblio_monitor_silence.example maintenance-window
```
